title: Social Media Creative
posterAlt: Film cover for Social Media Creative
role: Direction, Performance Direction, Cinematography and Post-Production
cardDescription: A social media piece directed and produced from capture through final delivery, with a controlled frame and typography shaped around the speaker's rhythm.
description: I directed and produced this social media piece from capture through final delivery, including performance direction, cinematography, lighting, camera operation, editing, sound design, motion graphics and color grading.

The visual approach was built around a controlled, intimate frame, using lighting and composition to give a simple talking-head setup more depth and character. During production, I directed the talent's delivery, pacing and presence on camera to achieve a more natural and intentional performance.

In post-production, I used pacing, typography and motion graphics to reinforce key moments in the speech rather than treating subtitles as a purely functional element. Changes in scale, typeface, position and emphasis help guide attention and maintain visual rhythm throughout the piece.

title: Why Do People Stay?
posterAlt: Film cover for Why Do People Stay?
role: Concept, Writing, Direction, Performance, Cinematography and Post-Production
cardDescription: A fully self-produced cinematic piece, written and performed in English and developed from the first idea through the final grade.
description: A fully self-produced cinematic piece. From the initial concept and script to directing, acting, cinematography, lighting and final post-production, every creative and technical aspect of this project was handled by me.

I designed the visual language, built the lighting setup, operated the camera, performed both characters, edited the narrative, created the typography and motion elements, designed the sound, and finished the project with a cinematic color grade.
The project was written and performed in English, adding another layer of creative and technical challenge to an independent production.

title: Beach Creative
role: Creative Direction, Performance Direction, Cinematography and Post-Production
cardDescription: A self-produced commercial creative shot on location with a minimal setup, using the beach and available light to shape the performance and images.
description: A fully self-produced commercial creative, developed and executed from capture to final delivery.
I was responsible for the production process, including creative direction, performance direction, cinematography, camera operation, lighting, shot composition and visual storytelling.

Working with a minimal production setup on location at the beach, I directed the talent's performance, movement and presence on camera, while designing the shots and visual approach around the environment and available natural light.
I also handled the complete post-production, including editing, pacing, sound design, color grading, transitions, visual effects and final image treatment.

title: Creative Adão
cardDescription: A project developed from the initial idea to the final cut, with production choices planned around how the material would work in the edit.
description: A project developed and executed entirely by me, from the initial idea to the final cut.
I was responsible for the concept, direction, performance direction, cinematography, lighting and camera operation, shaping both the visual approach and the performance on set.

The production was designed around deliberate framing, camera movement and lighting, using the location and the subject to build a stronger visual identity rather than simply documenting the performance.

I also handled the complete post-production, including editing, pacing, sound design, motion graphics and color grading. Each stage was approached as part of the same creative process, with decisions made during production already considering how the material would ultimately work in the edit.

title: Viral Short-Form
role: Research, Concept, Writing, Direction, Performance and Post-Production
cardDescription: A self-initiated project that turned a rapidly developing online topic into an original, narrative-driven short.
description: A self-initiated project created in response to a topic that was rapidly gaining attention online.

I identified the timing early and developed an original concept around it, turning a trending subject into a narrative-driven short rather than simply following the format of the content already circulating.

I handled the entire production, including research, concept development, writing, direction, performance, cinematography, lighting, camera operation, editing, sound design, motion graphics and color grading.

The piece was conceived and produced while the subject was still highly relevant, allowing the creative idea, execution and timing to work together. The video went on to reach a viral audience organically, making it an example of my ability to recognize cultural momentum and quickly turn it into original content.

title: Kasparov
role: Research, Concept, Writing, Direction and Post-Production
cardDescription: A personal project connecting a moment from Garry Kasparov's chess career with neuroscience and an everyday human experience.
description: A personal project built around a simple question: how do you turn an everyday human experience into a story worth watching?

I developed the concept by connecting a moment from Garry Kasparov's chess career with neuroscience and a behavior we experience in our daily lives. The historical reference became the foundation for a broader narrative, giving the subject context before bringing it back to something personal and familiar.
For the production, I brought in a friend and directed his performance, working on delivery, reactions and timing to make the scripted scenes feel natural on camera.

I was responsible for the full creative and technical process, including research, concept development, writing, direction, performance direction, cinematography, lighting, camera operation, editing, pacing, sound design, motion graphics and color grading.
The final piece combines original footage, performance and archival material to move between storytelling, history and science without losing the connection to the viewer's everyday experience.
